mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with the federal funds rate decline, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) reflects strong consumer demand, which can drive corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate decline does not result in positive S&P 500 returns, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong supply chain, which can lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE) and high payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment does not result in positive S&P 500 returns, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days if not accompanied by corresponding wage growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and S&P 500 returns are not negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates reduced demand in the housing market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in a late-cycle expansion regime.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by more than 5% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If housing starts decline by more than 5% quarter-over-quarter and S&P 500 returns are not negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a potential mismatch in monetary policy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the interaction between high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE does not result in negative S&P 500 returns, the hypothesis is falsified.
